requirements.requirement: On node1, schedule /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance to run every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: The final cron entry is exactly `15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance ...`; crond is active and enabled, and the executable schedule persisted across a verified reboot.

requirements.requirement: Retain the maintenance command's output in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log.
requirements.summary: The cron entry appends stdout and stderr to the requested log. Direct executions using that redirection produced retained output, and the log and its prior content remained present after reboot.

overall_summary: The requested daily 02:15 maintenance schedule and append-only log destination are established on node1 and survived a fully evidenced reboot. The executor also repaired the supplied malformed, non-executable command so the scheduled job can run.
limitations: No naturally triggered 02:15 cron execution was observed; successful output capture was demonstrated by manually invoking the same command with the configured redirection.

The attempted `crond -T` syntax check was unsupported on this system, so confidence relies on direct inspection of the conventional cron entry, active scheduler state, and successful command execution.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Repairing the prepared command was a necessary prerequisite because it was malformed and non-executable; creating the cron file implemented the task; manual log appends were bounded evidence collection; and the reboot supported the mandatory provider protocol. The unsuccessful `crond -T` validation was read-only. Final snapshots show no failed services, damaged package state, new network exposure, or abandoned temporary residue. Restart evidence is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID, and recovered crond, schedule, executable, and retained log.
